messages:
anya: Quick sync — weekend bring-up queue review. I added two intakes: ceres-40b (FP16 -> 8-bit quant experiments pending) and atlas-lite-13b-quant (already quantized, failing a couple eval slices). Need a prioritization call for next sprint. TL;DR: ceres has nice quality but big memory footprint; atlas-lite is cheap but shows ~3% QA regression on long-dialog tests.

devin: +1. Suggested gating checklist: basic perf bench, quant stability (3 restarts), safety/behavior smoke, and sample-set quality review. If any fail, we hold from canary.

luis: for perf bench I can run on the 8xA10 pool — when do you need results? I can turn on continuous traces.

anya: @luis asap — want throughput + p50/p99 on our convo workload, and token cost estimate. If it looks good we can schedule a canary.

samir: product perspective — roadmap has two infra tickets next sprint (latency optimizer + cache improvements). Cer es would benefit from cache work but atlas-lite could be a good short-term win for Dedicated. Recommend prioritizing atlas-lite if quant quality is fixable quickly.

devin: agree with roadmap tradeoff. But we should quantify user-impact: 3% regression on long dialog — is that edge-case or core? @eva can you share eval slices?

eva: I ran the eval set overnight. Quick paste of failure modes: hallucination increases on roleplay prompts, factual recall on >3-turn threads drops. Short prompts are fine. Sample scoring: 

```
model | overall | long_dialog | hallucination
atlas-lite-13b-quant | 0.87 | 0.72 | 0.18
atlas-lite-13b-fp16 | 0.90 | 0.85 | 0.05
ceres-40b-fp16 | 0.94 | 0.90 | 0.03
```

This suggests quantization cross-talk on KV cache or attention normalization.

luis: interesting — could be a kernel fusion/quant scale mismatch. I can repro a small example and log layerwise activation diffs. Need ~2 GPU-hours to dig in.

anya: Good. Let's use a lightweight priority rubric to decide what to bring up next sprint. Quick scoring (0-5 each): product-value, infra-risk, quant-risk, regression-impact. Add up.

devin: I'll draft scores: 
- ceres-40b: product-value 5, infra-risk 4, quant-risk 3, regression-impact 2 => total 14
- atlas-lite-13b-quant: product-value 3, infra-risk 2, quant-risk 4, regression-impact 3 => total 12

samir: I bump atlas-lite product-value to 4 because Dedicated customers asked for a cheaper option. New total 13.

anya: Updated table (quick):
```
Name | PV | IR | QR | RI | Total
ceres-40b | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 14
atlas-lite-13b-quant | 4 | 2 | 4 | 3 | 13
```
Looks like ceres edges out. But we should consider runway: ceres needs work on memory (maybe quant+sharding) and depends on cache/latency optimizer ticket. Atlas-lite might be unblockable if quant fix is quick.

devin: Proposal: 1) Run luis's activation diff for atlas-lite (2 GPUh). 2) If easy bug, prioritize atlas-lite for quick canary and Dedicated pilot. 3) Otherwise, schedule ceres bring-up and allocate quant-explore slot (4 GPUs) next sprint.

infra-bot: GPU reservation created: 2h on pool-a10 for luis (reservation id r-1745).

luis: Got the reservation, starting repro now. Will post logs in this thread and attach a short diff report.

eva: Also recommend adding a small automated eval slice to our canary pipeline that focuses on long-dialog factual checks. If it fails >2% relative to fp16 we abort rollout.

anya: Agreed. @devin can you add that slice to canary harness? Should be quick, two tests.

devin: Yup, will add tests and the abort rule. ETA tomorrow morning.

samir: From roadmap POV I'm ok with two-stage: quick attempt on atlas-lite, fallback to ceres if unresolved. Keep product informed.

anya: Thanks all — action items: luis run debug, devin add canary slice + abort rule, eva prepare short eval report for PMs, samir keep roadmap decisions. We'll reconvene Friday 10am to decide. :calendar: :thumbsup:
